title: Belichick denies loss of control as UNC investigation widens, September 7
dek: Bill Belichick said Monday that his UNC football program maintains an atmosphere of compliance, denying he has lost control amid an ongoing university investigation. General manager Michael Lombardi resigned September 3 after being placed on leave, and the investigation has expanded to include allegations of drug use and inappropriate relationships involving assistant coaches and recruiting staff.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: General manager Michael Lombardi resigned on September 3 after being placed on paid leave in late July as UNC's investigation expanded to include questions about drug use and inappropriate relationships among coaches and staff.
bottom_line: The scope and findings of the university's investigation will determine whether Belichick's claim of compliance holds. The September 11 home game against East Tennessee State will be his first full game-week news conference after the preliminary inquiry closes or expands further.
body:
Bill Belichick said Monday that his UNC football program "totally" maintains an atmosphere of rule compliance, denying he has lost institutional control amid an ongoing university investigation into the program's conduct. Reporters spent roughly the first 13 minutes of Belichick's 20-minute game week news conference asking questions about the investigation rather than the upcoming home game against East Tennessee State, according to the Guardian.
The investigation has deepened since Michael Lombardi, the program's general manager whom Belichick personally hired, was placed on paid administrative leave in late July following an HR complaint from a former employee. Lombardi resigned on September 3, according to the Guardian. Lombardi's attorney Tom Mars told The Athletic that the school's investigation now includes questions into potential "inappropriate" relationships that did not involve Lombardi, according to the Guardian. A separate reported by WRAL, cited by Front Office Sports, indicates the university's investigators asked about possible sexual relationships between assistant coaches and recruiting staff, and whether a member of UNC's recruiting staff had a sexual relationship with a player.
The investigation has also encompassed allegations regarding defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, Belichick's son.  Steve Belichick is currently on medical leave, per the Guardian.
When asked whether the university has asked him to change how he runs the program, Belichick said, "No. I have an ongoing relationship, communication with the university, and they've been very supportive, a great working relationship with those people." He added: "In the end, we want to run the program in the very best way. And if there's things we need to do to correct it, then we'll obviously do them." A UNC spokesman, Dean Stoyer, vice chancellor for communications, issued a statement: "The University continues to support Bill Belichick and the Carolina football program."
Belichick's contract mandates the veteran coach "promote an atmosphere of compliance" and maintain institutional control, per CBS Sports College Football. Belichick said he understands "the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team" and emphasized "our high standard here of our code of conduct and doing things the right way and making sure that our student-athletes are given the utmost, the best treatment, the very best care, and the very best coaching that we can possibly give them," according to CBS Sports. When asked if he saw such an atmosphere around him daily, Belichick said, "If you're around here every day, I think you'd see it."
The timing of the investigation is notable because it comes amid clear on-field and off-field dysfunction. In Belichick's debut season in 2025, the Tar Heels went 4 wins and 9 losses, with five double-digit losses, per the Guardian. An assistant coach was briefly suspended for violating NCAA rules that year, per the Guardian. UNC defeated TCU 15-10 in its season opener on August 29 in Week 0 in Dublin, Ireland, avoiding an 0-1 start. Running back Benjamin Hall said Monday: "We're so focused on everything internal and getting better on the field and getting better in the meeting room that we could care less about what we see in the headlines or what's on the news. It's not going to affect this team," according to the Guardian.
Belichick is 74 years old and won six Super Bowl titles as head coach of the New England Patriots. He is in the second season of a five-year, $50 million contract with the Tar Heels, per CBS Sports. The program has "redistributed some things" following Lombardi's leave and resignation, with "no updates" on a replacement, per Front Office Sports.
